l.i: Quò tua te virtus, quò pia fata vocant.
Nil furor invidia te terreat: illa decorum
Insequitur pleno, corpỹ ut umbra, gradu.
Atq; inde auxiliū, si tonat aura, pete.
Nil metuat curétve, sibi mens conscia recti; S-
ed locet in Domino spem, toleréts, suâ.
His Genii tacitis animatus rite fusurris,

main_text.l: Livor ei triplicè quamvis induceret hostè,
Malleo et instaret vehemès affliction trino,
Sustinuit tamen, & divina fultus opis spe

l.i: In Domino pariter qui fidit, despicit hostes,
Gaudétque in tacito, forte tonante, sinu.

page.notes: Woodcut ornament between text and catchword, not transcribed. Several words are written with an apparent s-like form; long s rendered as s. Line "affliction" printed as "afflictio" and "Malleo" line and "fultus opis spe" line have a word split across the line end with a stray tail; treated as printed. Ligature forms like "s" in "sinu" and the tails on "Sed locet" and "Gaudét" are typographical. The line "Livor ei triplicè" begins roman, italic continues; verse is set with mixed roman and italic words as printed. Heading "PIRCKHEYMERE" is the printed name in capitals, mixed with italic "bonis" and roman "pulcherrimè". Doubtful: "toleréts" (printed as tolerét with a sign), "corpỹ" (nasal mark), "Gegen" catchword may be incomplete.
